questions.question: Washing machine dryer works on the principle of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's first law.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A washing machine dryer entirely works upon the principle of the law of inertia.**

 
 
• To dry clothes, the drum of the washing machine dryer is subjected to motion, which further causes the clothes to move.
 
• However, the water molecules contained in the cloth do not follow the motion and stay at their position of rest. 
 
• Due to the gravitational pull of the earth, the water gets collected at the base of the drum.
 
• The holes of the drum let the water out. leaving the clothes dry.
 
 
 
• **Newton's first law **is also called the** law of inertia**.
 
 
• **It states that if a body is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless it is acted upon by a force.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's second law **defines a force to be equal to a change in momentum per change in time.

 
 
• It's also called the law of motion.
 
• Examples: riding a bicycle, hitting a ball, pushing a car etc.
 
 
 
• **Newton's third law states** that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
• Examples: a horse pulls a cart, a person walks on the ground, a hammer pushes a nail etc.

questions.question: Which of the following converts glucose into glycogen (a complex carbohydrate used for storage) and amino acids into proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ ​Liver.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **
Key Points__**

__
 
• The biochemical process in which glucose is converted into glycogen in the liver is known as **g****lycogenesis**__.
 
• The liver** converts glucose into glycogen (a complex carbohydrate used for storage) and amino acids into proteins.
 
• The cell must have an excess of glucose for starting this process.
 
• Glucose is the starting molecule and is converted through the process of glycogenesis.
 
• When the body does not have readily available glucose, the body creates glycogen through the process of glycogenesis.
 
• This process is activated during rest periods in the liver and also activated by insulin in response to high levels of glucose.
 
• When the body gets an excess meal and the blood glucose levels are high, the pancreas releases insulin hormone to store glucose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Glycogenolysis:

 
 
• Glycogenolysis is the breakdown of the molecule glycogen into glucose.
 
• Glycogenolysis occurs in muscle and liver cells when more energy needs to be produced. 
 
 
 
• Gluconeogenesis:
 
 
• Gluconeogenesis is a process that transforms non-carbohydrate substrates (such as lactate, amino acids, and glycerol) into glucose.
 
• Gluconeogenesis takes place in the liver and kidneys. Gluconeogenic substrates include glycerol, lactate, propionate, and certain amino acids. 
 
 
 
• Glycolysis:
 
 
• Glycolysis is a cytoplasmic pathway that breaks down glucose into two three-carbon compounds and generates energy.
 
• This process occurs in the cytosol of the cell cytoplasm. Glycolysis is an oxygen-independent metabolic pathway.

questions.question: The study of tissues is called
questions.solution:
The study of tissues is called __**Histology**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Histology** is the branch of biology that studies the microscopic structure of tissues.
 
• Tissues are groups of cells that work together to perform a specific function, and histology helps in understanding their structure and function.
 
• Histology is essential in medical research and diagnosis, as it helps in identifying abnormalities in tissues that can indicate diseases.
 
• This field uses various techniques such as staining and microscopy to observe the fine details of tissue architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Histopathology** is a related field that involves the microscopic examination of tissue in order to study the manifestations of disease.
 
• The study of histology began in the 19th century with the advent of the microscope, which allowed scientists to observe cells and tissues in greater detail than ever before.
 
• Histology plays a crucial role in the fields of pathology, anatomy, and biology, providing insights into the complex organization of tissues in both health and disease.
 
• The knowledge gained from histological studies is applied in various medical fields, including oncology, neurology, and immunology.

questions.question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The energy of light is** inversely proportional** to its wavelength.
 
• Therefore, the light with the **longest wavelength,** i.e. **red**, has the **least energy.**
 
• The colours of VIBGYOR are arranged in **increasing order** of their** wavelengths.**
 
• Hence, **violet** has the** highest energy **and red has the least.
 
• **Green** is the colour of light with a wavelength between yellow and blue.
 
• It has **more energy** than yellow but less than blue.
 
• **Yellow** is the colour of light with a wavelength between green and orange.
 
• It has** less energy** than green but more than orange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **VIBGYOR** stands for** Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red.**

 
 
• These are the** seven colours **of the visible spectrum of light.
 
 
 
• Violet has the **shortest wavelength** and the highest energy among the colours of VIBGYOR.
 
• **Indigo** is a colour that lies between **blue and violet **in the spectrum.
 
 
• It is not always distinguishable from blue and is **not** considered a separate colour by some people.
 
 
 
• **Orange** is a colour that lies between **yellow and red** in the spectrum.
 
 
• It has **more energy** than red but less than yellow.

questions.question: The remains of Great Bath have been found from the excavation at which of the following Harappan sites?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjodaro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Bath was discovered at the archaeological site of **Mohenjodaro**, one of the most prominent sites of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Mohenjodaro is located in the Sindh province of present-day **Pakistan**.
 
• The Great Bath is one of the best-known structures among the ruins of Mohenjodaro and is believed to have been used for ritualistic purposes.
 
• This structure measures approximately **12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep** and is made of baked bricks.
 
• The Great Bath is an early example of **public water management** and intricate hydraulic engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**

 
 
• Also known as the Harappan Civilization, it flourished around 2500 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It is noted for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• Key sites include Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
 
 
• **Mohenjodaro**
 
 
• It was one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilization and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• The city featured a well-planned grid layout, advanced drainage system, and standardized brick sizes.
 
• Mohenjodaro means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.
 
 
 
• **Great Bath**
 
 
• It is considered one of the earliest public water tanks in the ancient world.
 
• The structure had a layer of natural bitumen to make it waterproof.
 
• Steps at either end of the bath indicate that it was used for ceremonial bathing.
 
 
 
• **Excavation of Mohenjodaro**
 
 
• The site was first discovered by R. D. Banerji in 1922.
 
• Subsequent excavations were carried out by John Marshall, Ernest Mackay, and others.
 
• Excavations revealed a wealth of artifacts including pottery, tools, and seals.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be considered as a health infrastructure indicator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cost of living.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Health infrastructure indicators refer to factors that measure the availability and accessibility of healthcare facilities and services in a particular region or country.**
 
• indicators as they reflect the quality of healthcare and public health interventions in a given population.
 
• Cost of living, on the other hand, is not a health infrastr** Maternal mortality, infant mortality, and life expectancy are all examples of health infrastructureucture **indicator as it is a measure of the general economic conditions and living standards of a population, which may indirectly affect healthcare outcomes but is not a direct measure of healthcare infrastructure.
 
• Maternal mortality refers to the number of deaths of women due to pregnancy-related complications, while infant mortality refers to the number of deaths of infants before their first birthday. Both indicators are important measures of the quality of maternal and child healthcare services.
 
• Life expectancy is a measure of the average age to which people in a particular population are expected to live, and is influenced by a range of factors including healthcare, nutrition, and lifestyle. It is an important indicator of overall population health and well-being.

questions.question: Where is the Rakhigarhi Indus Valley site located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rakhigarhi is one of the largest and most significant Indus Valley Civilization sites, located in the Hisar district of **Haryana**, India.
 
• It is considered one of the five major urban centers of the Indus Valley Civilization, alongside Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, and Ganweriwala.
 
• The site dates back to approximately 2600–1900 BCE, with evidence of both Pre-Harappan and Mature Harappan phases.
 
• Rakhigarhi spans over 350 hectares, comprising seven mounds labeled RGR-1 to RGR-7, showcasing extensive urban planning and advanced societal structures.
 
• Excavations have revealed a planned settlement with streets, drainage systems, storage structures, pottery, jewelry, and even human burials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC):**

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban cultures, flourishing around 2500–1900 BCE.
 
• It was characterized by advanced urban planning, including grid-pattern cities, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures.
 
• Key sites include Harappa (Punjab, Pakistan), Mohenjo-daro (Sindh, Pakistan), Dholavira (Gujarat, India), and Rakhigarhi (Haryana, India).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Rakhigarhi:**
 
 
• Rakhigarhi has provided crucial insights into the daily life, trade, and burial practices of the Harappans.
 
• In 2022, DNA analysis on remains from Rakhigarhi indicated a local genetic continuity, supporting the indigenous development of the civilization.
 
• The site is included in the tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
 
 
 
• **Key Findings at Rakhigarhi:**
 
 
• Artifacts like terracotta figurines, seals, pottery, and tools highlight trade and craftsmanship.
 
• Burials with grave goods, such as ornaments and tools, suggest belief in an afterlife and social stratification.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Efforts are ongoing to preserve the site under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
 
• A proposed museum at Rakhigarhi will showcase the site's history and findings.

questions.question: Which glands help in digestion in the stomach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gastric glands**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gastric glands** are responsible for aiding digestion in the stomach.
 
• These glands secrete gastric juice, which contains hydrochloric acid and digestive enzymes such as pepsin.
 
• The hydrochloric acid creates an acidic environment that helps in breaking down food, and the enzyme pepsin breaks down proteins into peptides.
 
• Gastric glands are located in the lining of the stomach and play a crucial role in the digestive process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gastric glands** are composed of different types of cells, including parietal cells, chief cells, and mucous cells.
 
• **Parietal cells** secrete hydrochloric acid, which helps in killing bacteria and activating pepsinogen to pepsin.
 
• **Chief cells** produce pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of pepsin.
 
• **Mucous cells** secrete mucus to protect the stomach lining from the harsh acidic environment.
 
• Malfunction or diseases affecting the gastric glands can lead to digestive issues such as ulcers and gastritis.

questions.question: Babur introduced a technique of warfare called '____' which divided the army into different divisions to flank the enemy from all sides.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tulughma**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The new war tactics introduced by Babur were the** tulughma and the araba.**
 
• Tulughma meant dividing the whole army into various units, viz. the **Left, the Right and the Centre.**
 
• The Left and Right divisions were further subdivided into Forward and Rear divisions.
 
• Through this a small army could be used to surround the **enemy from all the sides.**
 
• The Centre Forward division was then provided with carts (araba) which were placed in rows facing the enemy and tied to each other with animal hide ropes.
 
• Behind them were placed cannons protected and supported by **mantelets **which could be used to **easily manoeuvre the canons. **
 
• These two tactics made** Babur’s artillery lethal.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• The First Battle of Panipat (21 April 1526) fought near a small village of Panipat Haryana.
 
• The battle was fought between the invading forces of Zahir-ud-din Babur and Lodi Empire during the rule of Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• The Mughal forces of Babur, the ruler of Kabulistan, defeated ruling army of Ibrahim Lodi, Sultan of Delhi.
 
• Babur’s tactics of *Tulughma and Araba *__that led him to victory.

questions.question: What is the new feature launched by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation for Universal Account Numbers (UAN) activation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aadhaar-based face authentication.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **EPFO has launched Aadhaar-based face authentication for the generation and activation of UANs through the UMANG app.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The new system enables employees to generate and activate their UANs independently in a secure and contactless manner using Aadhaar-based face authentication.**
 
• Face authentication ensures tamper-proof identity verification and reduces errors, eliminating employer or regional office intervention.
 
• Aadhaar details are auto-filled and verified during the process, with UAN activation completed instantly.
 
• The EPFO aims to use the technology for digital life certificates and plans to assist pensioners via volunteers from My Bharat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• UMANG App__

 __
 
• The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app is a government platform that provides access to a variety of services, including EPFO services, using a single interface.
 
 
 
• Jeevan Pramaan__
 __
 
• Jeevan Pramaan is a biometric-enabled digital service to issue life certificates for pensioners, reducing the need for physical visits to pension-disbursing agencies.
 
 
 
• Aadhaar__
 
 
• Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identification number issued by the government of India to residents based on biometric and demographic data.
